_notes: Every word and number on screen or in the voice-over lives in this file.
maxSeconds is the platform's ceiling for the rendered MP4 including every pad; the composition refuses to build and stills.mjs fails loudly when the scenes exceed it.
Scenes marked optional:true are dropped automatically while their image is missing from public/img (run assets.sh after docs/presentation/ changes).
voiceName: the Gemini text-to-speech voice voice.sh asks for.
voiceTempo: the generated voice files are time-stretched by this factor (ffmpeg atempo, pitch kept) by voice.sh, so the same words fit the ceiling; 1.0 leaves them as spoken.
Scene duration = the voice file's length + padSeconds; voice.sh regenerates public/voice/<id>.wav from the voice lines below.

timelapse: public/img/<dir>/NN.png from `from` to `to`, played once across the scene, so the frame rate follows the voice line; assets.sh copies docs/presentation/session and docs/presentation/stages, placeholders.sh builds stand-ins from a run directory.

Terminal blocks: cmd (the host's question, typed), note (assistant prose), call (a scry tool call with trimmed result lines), answer (markdown-ish: **bold**, `code`, ## heading; a leading 4-space indent keeps the line in place), meta (a dim footer line). keyCitations are drawn orange, every other id blue.

Frame cut-in: src is the image in docs/presentation/, width/height its pixel size, zoom the point (image pixels) the slow zoom moves towards and the final scale (the view never leaves the image), labels are pinned to image pixels and drawn in screen space.

scenes.caption: Screen recordings you can search
scenes.voice: Scry turns a screen recording into a hierarchical index of what happened on screen, and any AI agent can ask it questions over MCP.

lines: Yes, all three saved. In each case the portal showed the profile-specific success toast and the endpoint table went from one row to two, with the new AFDEndpoint row present. I looked at the three post-save frames myself.

**tm-profile-ap** · frame 22, 64.0 s · toast "Saved Traffic Manager profile changes" / "Successfully saved configuration changes to Traffic Manager profile 'tm-profile-ap'" (22:b55, b58, b60) · new row AFDEndpoint, Disabled, Disabled, External endpoint, weight 1 (22:b91, b89, b93) · "Showing 1 - 2 of 2 results." (22:b112), up from 1 of 1 at frame 21 (21:b127)

**tm-profile-EU** · frame 45, 132.2 s · same toast naming 'tm-profile-EU' (45:b61, b64, b66) · AFDEndpoint, Disabled, Disabled, External endpoint, weight 1 (45:b98, b97, b99) · 2 of 2 (45:b119), up from the single eu.endpoint row at T36

**tm-profile-NA** · frame 52, 151.7 s · same toast naming 'tm-profile-NA' (52:b62, b65, b67) · AFDEndpoint, Disabled, Disabled, External endpoint, weight 1 (52:b96, b97) · 2 of 2 (52:b118), up from 1 of 1 at frame 50 (50:b130)

**Saved, but disabled.** Every new row reads Disabled with weight 1, matching the unchecked Enable Endpoint box. The additions took effect, but the endpoint receives no traffic in this state, and nothing in the video enables it.

scenes.caption: Index once, ask forever
scenes.voice: Indexing this session cost about seventy-five cents on an open model. The index is plain, hierarchical text; the video is never needed again. Index once, ask forever.

scenes.caption: 1. Read: OCR boxes on every piece of text, full resolution
scenes.voice: First it reads every piece of text on every frame at full resolution.

scenes.caption: 2. Track: what appeared, changed or vanished between frames; every text gets a lifetime
scenes.voice: Then it tracks what appeared, changed or vanished, so every text has a lifetime.

scenes.caption: 3. Label: windows, popups, and which label goes with which value
scenes.voice: Then a model labels windows, popups, and which label goes with which value.

scenes.caption: 4. Interpret: what each change did, and whether it was submitted
scenes.voice: Then it records what each change did, and whether it was submitted.

scenes.caption: text · frames · changes · steps · sections · session
scenes.voice: All of it becomes one index at six levels: every text, every frame, every change and what it meant, steps, sections, the whole session. Search at any level; every entry cites its frames.
